question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & k & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & k \\ k & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$. For what values of $k$ does $|A| = 0$?
explanation:
Compute the determinant:
$|A| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & k & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & k \\ k & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$
Expanding along row 1:
$= 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & k \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} - k\begin{vmatrix}1 & k \\ k & 1\end{vmatrix} + 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ k & 1\end{vmatrix}$
Now,
$\begin{vmatrix}1 & k \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1 - k$
$\begin{vmatrix}1 & k \\ k & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1 - k^2$
$\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ k & 1\end{vmatrix} = 1 - k$
So,
$|A| = (1-k) - k(1 - k^2) + (1 - k) = (2-2k) - k(1 - k^2)$
$= 2 - 2k - k + k^3 = k^3 - 3k + 2$
Set $=0$:
$k^3 - 3k + 2 = 0$
Factor: $(k-1)^2(k+2)=0 \implies k=1\;(repeated);\;-2$
